newsitem.title: UK: Russia debt price stumbles on Yeltsin health news.
newsitem.headline: Russia debt price stumbles on Yeltsin health news.

text.p: Prices of Russian debt fell on Wednesday in reaction to news that President Boris Yeltsin's illness was serious though his condition had stabilised significantly.
By midday, dollar Vneshekonombank paper -- former Soviet foreign commercial debt which Moscow is in the throes of restructuring -- had dropped half a point to 77-1/2 cents in the dollar.
The price later crept back a little and some traders said the statement from Moscow added little to what was already known.
The chief Kremlin doctor told a news conference in Moscow that the 65-year-old president's condition had stabilised significantly, but he added pneumonia was serious and could involve complications.

"We really need more information. That fact that it is serious is what we have been assuming," one debt trader said, adding that the positive tone overall for the market should help support Russian prices.
Prices are currently at the lower end of the range they have been trading in since mid-October.

Analysts believe Russia's economic reforms would continue without Yeltsin in power, but some are concerned there might be problems in running the country if he were not to recover fully and linger in office, only just able to carry out his duties.

Until the state of his health becomes clearer, prices are bound to be more volatile, traders said. "With Russian debt at the moment, you have got to be fairly agile and not take too long a view," one trader said.
